title: Warp: Print Mockups

candidates.name: Warp: Print Mockups
candidates.why: Carrier plus the job noun a print-on-demand seller actually types. Warp is both the textile term and the real operation this app performs, a flat design warped onto a woven garment, so the carrier describes the wedge rather than decorating it; Print Mockups is the searched head term and is counted as part of the name, not of the carrier.

candidates.name: Printfold
candidates.why: Compact, ownable and easy to spell after hearing it once, but it leaves out the head term a seller searches for, so it spends the strongest ranking field on a word nobody types and needs its whole discovery budget bought with ads.

candidates.name: Mockforge
candidates.why: Coins cleanly and is distinctive, but an English reader hears mock as ridicule rather than as a mockup, and the word carries no textile or printing meaning, so it describes nothing about the job it names.

candidates.name: Drape
candidates.why: Evokes fabric strongly and reads well at 48dp, but a one-word evocative title with no job noun is unsearchable for what the app does, and on this shelf the seller is looking for a mockup rather than for cloth.

candidates.name: Product Mockup Studio
candidates.why: States the job plainly and is legal, but it is a generic phrase with no carrier to distinguish it, so it competes for the same words as the 500K+ incumbent without offering the searcher a reason to prefer it.

candidates.name: Ghost Draft
candidates.why: Ties the name to the ghost-mannequin garment shot, which is evocative but promises a specific form this plan deliberately does not build: the ghost-mannequin operation has no endpoint and no price, so the name would advertise a capability the app cannot honour.

candidates.name: Mockup Generator
candidates.why: The negative control: the bare category head term the shelf's 500K+ leaders already own, which Google itself says does not improve ranking, and the exact generic phrase the naming methodology forbids as a title rather than as a job description.

rejected.name: Mockup Generator
rejected.reason: Bare category head term, and the negative control of the field: it is the phrase the 500K+ incumbent already ranks for, Google states unnecessary keywords do not help ranking, and it names the category instead of the wedge this app has.

rejected.name: Printfold
rejected.reason: Lost on discoverability rather than on art: it drops the head term a seller actually types, so every install it wins has to be bought with ads instead of earned by a title that contains the searched words.

rejected.name: Ghost Draft
rejected.reason: Names a capability this plan refuses to build, because the ghost-mannequin operation carries no endpoint and no price in the factory's own capability inventory, and a title must not promise what the app cannot do.

audience: One-person print-on-demand, merch and digital-download shops on Etsy, eBay, Depop, Vinted, Amazon Merch and small Shopify stores, producing listing imagery for designs they have finished but not yet printed.
rationale: A carrier plus the real two-to-three-word job noun is the methodology's recommended shape for a small focused tool: Warp is the true textile operation the app performs, and Print Mockups is the term a seller types into Play, so one title carries both the wedge and the demand.
collisionCheck: UNVERIFIED. This scan did not run a Play title search and did not query any trademark register. The decider is a Google Play search for the exact title plus a class-9 search of TMview, USPTO, EUIPO and WIPO for Warp and its close variants; a clean search is not legal clearance, and a Cloudflare product named WARP is a known non-Play collision.
localisationCheck: Nineteen characters in en-US and eighteen in ru-RU, so both declared locales clear Play's thirty-character cap with eleven or more characters of slack, and neither is a machine translation. The Latin carrier and job noun carry into both locales, but whether a Russian-speaking seller discovers an English job noun is unmeasured and needs a native review before the listing is written.
